title: What auditors, the budget analyst, grand juries and the State Auditor concluded about results
question: When an outside reviewer looked at whether these programmes work, what did it conclude?
finding: 17 reviews issued between 2018 and 2026 reach the same conclusion from different directions: the City mostly counts activity, not results, and in several departments could not say which providers were effective. None of them found that a programme does not work; they found that the records needed to tell were missing, inconsistent or unverified.
how: Audits, assessments and grand-jury reports on disk that deal with programme results were read. Each row gives the programme, the conclusion restated in plain words, and one short quotation, which the script checks is present word for word in the saved text of the document before the row is kept.
limits: One sentence cannot carry a whole report, and most of these reports also record progress and the department's reply. Several are years old and the departments have since changed their contracts and measures; the homelessness department adopted standard measures in 2021 and a new plan in 2023. Grand-jury reports are the work of citizen volunteers, not professional auditors. The State Auditor report on homelessness funding examined the State and two other cities, not San Francisco.
